content.value_statement: Slow Python code is hard to fix without clear measurements. This skill guides profiling, benchmarking, memory tuning, and targeted optimization work.
actual_capabilities: Explains CPU profiling with cProfile, pstats, line_profiler, and py-spy.
Shows benchmark patterns with timeit, decorators, and pytest-benchmark.
Compares common Python data structure and loop optimization approaches.
Covers memory optimization with generators, tracemalloc, weak references, and slots.
Provides examples for async I/O, multiprocessing, and database query tuning.
Includes a performance checklist for profiling before and after changes.
limitations: It is guidance only and does not run profilers automatically.
Example timings are illustrative and may differ on real hardware.
It does not replace production observability or load testing.
Some examples require optional packages such as NumPy, py-spy, or pytest-benchmark.

use_cases.title: Diagnose a Slow Endpoint
use_cases.description: Find CPU, I/O, or database bottlenecks before changing application code.

use_cases.title: Reduce Memory Pressure
use_cases.description: Use generators, tracemalloc, and object layout changes to lower memory usage.

use_cases.title: Validate Optimization Work
use_cases.description: Create repeatable benchmarks and compare before and after performance results.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Bottleneck
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me profile this Python function and identify the most likely bottleneck before changing the code.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Memory Use
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Python workflow for memory waste and suggest generator, iterator, or allocation improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Benchmark Alternatives
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a fair benchmark for these Python implementations and explain which measurements matter.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Production Profiling
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a safe profiling plan for this Python service, including tools, metrics, risks, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: A function spends too long processing a large list.
output_examples.output: The skill would suggest timing the function, profiling cumulative time, and checking list copies before proposing targeted changes.

output_examples.input: A web service slows down during external API calls.
output_examples.output: The skill would compare synchronous and async I/O behavior, then recommend measuring latency, concurrency, and error handling.

output_examples.input: A database import job commits each row separately.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend batching inserts, measuring commit overhead, and validating correctness after the performance change.

best_practices: Measure first, then optimize the slowest proven path.
Benchmark with representative input sizes and repeatable environments.
Keep readability unless profiling shows a clear performance need.
anti_patterns: Do not optimize code based only on intuition.
Do not compare benchmarks with different inputs or environments.
Do not introduce concurrency before confirming the workload is I/O-bound or CPU-bound.

faq.question: Does this skill execute profiling tools for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples that users can run in their own environment.

faq.question: Which Python profilers does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers cProfile, pstats, line_profiler, memory_profiler, tracemalloc, py-spy, and pytest-benchmark.

faq.question: Can it help with production performance issues?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains production profiling concepts, but users must follow their own access and safety controls.

faq.question: Does it support database optimization?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for batch inserts, indexing, query planning, and selecting only needed columns.

faq.question: Is this only for CPU-bound code?
faq.answer: No. It also covers memory usage, async I/O, multiprocessing, database access, and benchmarking.

faq.answer: Yes. The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
